verses.text: Follow my example, as I follow the example of Christ.
I praise you for remembering me in everything, and for holding on to the teachings I passed on to you.
But I want you to understand that Christ is the head of every man, the man is the head of the woman, and God is the head of Christ.
Every man who prays or speaks God's message with his head covered brings shame on his head.
But every woman who prays or speaks God's message with her head uncovered brings shame on her head. It is the same as having her head shaved.
If a woman will not cover her head, she should cut her hair short. But if it is shameful for a woman to cut her hair or shave her head, she should cover her head.
A man should not cover his head, because he is the image and glory of God. But the woman is the glory of the man.
For man did not come from woman, but woman came from man.
And man was not created for woman, but woman for man.
That is why a woman should have a sign of authority on her head, because of the angels.
But in the Lord, woman needs man and man needs woman.
For as woman came from man, so also man is born of woman. And everything comes from God.
Judge for yourselves. Is it right for a woman to pray to God with her head uncovered?
Does nature itself not teach you that long hair is a shame for a man?
But long hair is a woman's glory. Her hair is given to her as a covering.
If anyone wants to argue about this, we have no other practice, and neither do the churches of God.
In the following things I do not praise you. When you meet together, you do more harm than good.
First, I hear that when you meet as a church, there are divisions among you, and I believe some of it.
No doubt there have to be differences among you, to show which of you have God's approval.
When you meet together, it is not really the Lord's Supper you eat.
For as you eat, some of you go ahead with your own meal. One person stays hungry, and another gets drunk.
Do you not have homes to eat and drink in? Or do you look down on God's church and shame those who have nothing? What shall I say to you? Shall I praise you? No, I will not praise you for this!
For I received from the Lord what I also passed on to you. On the night he was betrayed, the Lord Jesus took bread.
He gave thanks, broke it and said, "This is my body, which is given for you. Do this to remember me."
In the same way, after supper he took the cup and said, "This cup is the new covenant made in my blood. Whenever you drink it, do this to remember me."
For whenever you eat this bread and drink this cup, you are telling about the Lord's death until he comes.
So whoever eats the bread or drinks the Lord's cup in a wrong way will be guilty of sinning against the body and blood of the Lord.
Everyone should look closely at themselves before they eat the bread and drink from the cup.
For anyone who eats and drinks without seeing the meaning of the Lord's body eats and drinks judgement on themselves.
That is why many of you are weak and sick, and some of you have died.
But if we judged ourselves rightly, we would not come under judgement.
When the Lord judges us, he is correcting us, so that we will not be condemned with the world.
So, my brothers and sisters, when you meet to eat, wait for each other.
If anyone is hungry, they should eat at home, so that your meetings do not bring judgement on you. I will give more instructions about the other things when I come.
